Saxophonist and band leader Dave Pell has had a variety of jobs in the music world. A native of New York, he was born in 1925 and made the move to the west coast in the late 40s. Dave was employed by Bob Crosby and Les Brown, learning skills that would enable him to lead the very successful Dave Pell Octet. This ensemble found a commercial niche in the jazz market and featured sidemen included Benny Carter, Pepper Adams and Art Pepper. He has worked as a producer for a number of record labels, and his photography has graced the album covers of numerous artists. Dave was instrumental in producing The Prez Conference, a tribute to Lester Young, and his boundless energy keeps him busy on numerous musical (and golfing) projects.
Dave was interviewed by Monk Rowe before a performance by The Prez Conference at the Sarasota Jazz Festival on April 11, 1996.

We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. My name is Monk Rowe, and it’s a great pleasure to have Dave Pell with us. Saxophonist and photographer, record producer, publisher. All of those things.

A lot of hats. A lot of interests. And all coming from music so it’s all surrounded in that creative world of our dreams of being able to play in bands and being able to play and enjoy. And it’s been a lot of fun.
